hippăgōgi , ōrum (Gr. acc.-gūs,
I. v. infra ), f., = ἱππαγωγοί, vessels for transporting horses, cavalry-transports: “quinque et triginta naves, quas hippagogus vocant, ab Elea profectae, cum equitibus Gallis equisque,” Liv. 44, 28, 7 ; cf. hippagines and hippegus.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
